title: Exact descent of tensoring with a fixed K-flat complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ its abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For every K-flat complex $A$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the functors $B\mapsto A\otimes_R B$ and $B\mapsto B\otimes_R A$ preserve all quasi-isomorphisms and descend to exact functors $D(R)\to D(R)$, canonically identified with $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QA$. Their coherent integer-shift comparisons are the localization of the signed total-complex maps in [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. They take cone triangles to distinguished triangles including the connecting map. Shifts preserve K-flatness and flat terms. On the full derived tensor bifunctor, chain maps between flat-term K-flat fixed arguments, and all derived maps obtained by their localization, induce transformations commuting with shifts in the varying argument; both orders of extracting shifts retain the signed compatibility of that leaf. No boundedness or flatness of cohomology is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); explicit cone and localization argument with the convention of derived.tex definition-cone and definition-distinguished-triangle. Signed shifts: more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs] to the given $A$. It supplies the two additive homotopy tensor functors, the cone isomorphisms with their $-p_u$ equations, and preservation of every quasi-isomorphism. Its last clause gives $A[n]$ K-flat with flat terms, so the resolving subcategory is stable under shifts. In particular no condition on the endpoints of a quasi-isomorphism or on cohomology flatness has entered.

proof.text: Use these homotopy exactness and inversion conclusions as the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-tensor-localization-comparison]. This yields additive exact $G_A,G^A$ with the localized coherent signed shifts and representative comparisons. The normalized isomorphisms $d_L,d_R$ identify them with the specified $T(QA,-),T(-,QA)$; their composite comparisons agree exactly with the published representative comparison on every resolving object. Their resolution formulas also specify those composites on arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and the construction immediately before it); the comparison is with the published resolving comparison of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent. Localization of functors and transformations: categories.tex lemma-properties-left-localization and lemma-properties-right-localization; cone convention: derived.tex definition-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: The shift-stability from Step 1 permits [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent] for this same published $T$. It gives one coherent shift structure on the entire bifunctor and the mixed $(-1)^{ab}$ identity. Its normalization clause applies to the composite comparisons of Step 2, so those comparisons commute with the shifts on every varying object. Thus the restrictions of this single bifunctor structure coincide with the exact one-variable structures, and the exactness of $G_A,G^A$ gives the asserted exactness of $T(QA,-),T(-,QA)$, including the third arrow of each localized cone triangle. Finally, the naturality assertion of the same node applies to every derived fixed-argument map, hence also to the indicated chain maps and inverses. All three lemmas allow unbounded complexes.
